notes:
- Company: BuildBench.io — developer tooling startup building a hosted CI/IDE companion. Interested in low-latency streaming for build logs and function-calling agents to run tests/lints in a sandbox.
- Primary ask: run user-initiated test runs (unit + integration) and linters via an LLM-driven agent that can call functions to spin ephemeral containers, execute test suites, collect artifacts, and stream logs back to the IDE.
- Security: "ephemeral execution only, no persistent workspace; all artifacts go to customer S3 with retention rules" — security team emphasized. Need KMS integration and per-run audit events.
- Performance: requires sub-500ms first-byte for log streaming (IDE UX) and <200ms token latency for completions. Throughput: spikey during nightly e2e runs (50 concurrent jobs).
- Model/versioning: wants model pinning per-project, ability to route to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical completions, and strict fallback policy for outages.
- POC scope: 1) demonstrate function-calling to create ephemeral runner; 2) execute tests + linters; 3) stream logs with incremental flushes to IDE; 4) produce signed audit log entry per run.
- Quote from CTO: "We need to be 100% sure the agent cannot access host kernel or customer secrets — strict sandboxing is non-negotiable."
- Notes on cost sensitivity: willing to pay for dedicated capacity if predictable; concerned about unit cost for long-running integration tests.
- Integration points: GitHub Apps, internal auth (SSO), internal artifact store (S3), CI orchestration hooks.
- Next: schedule infra/security architecture review w/ Redwood eng (SE + infra), finalize SOW.
